To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
algorithmic authority is an emergent form of social authority in which algorithms are increasingly able to affect everyday life through automated decision-making.
algorithms are becoming a source of authority and are increasingly being used to manage and interpret human activity.

1) algorithmic authority has a significant impact on the economy, politics, and society; 2) algorithms can be designed to have positive or negative impacts on the economy, society, and politics; 3) the design and implementation of algorithms is a complex process and can have unintended consequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
algorithmic authority in four key domains: (1) quantified self and personal informatics, (2) healthcare, (3) digital labor and the sharing economy, and (4) social media and the news.
the ways that algorithms and big data are used to interpret, decide, and manage everyday practices and the implications for the ethics, politics and economics of algorithmically managed life.
the ways in which algorithmic authority is manifested, the ways in which it is resisted, the ways in it is challenged, and the ways in which its authority is legitimized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
algorithms are becoming more and more powerful and are being used in a variety of ways to make decisions, manage people and information, and interpret data.
algorithms have the ability to influence and affect human action and behavior, as well as the ability to influence the accessibility of information.

the use of algorithms in the workplace is a positive development, but it is important to consider the ethical implications of their use and to ensure that they are used responsibly and in a way that is beneficial to all parties involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
algorithms are increasingly becoming the gatekeepers of access to information, the evaluators of human performance and worth, and the managers of everyday life.
we are interested in the ways in which the power of algorithms is being used to manage and influence everyday life, work, and economic systems.
we are concerned with the ways that the power of algorithms and data is used to control and manage human action and information access.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the authority of algorithmic decision-making has become increasingly opaque, and that the power of algorithms is often wielded in ways that are not transparent to those affected.
algorithmic authority is a complex and multi-faceted phenomenon that needs to be understood in the context of its particular social, cultural, political and economic environment.

algorithmic authority is not only about the power of algorithms over users, but also about the power of algorithmic systems to shape the way we think and act, as well as to influence the way we are perceived by others.
